title: Safety Audits and Findings by SAF Inspector-General’s Office and Improvement Measures Implemented
what_it_is: Safety Audits and Findings by SAF Inspector-General’s Office and Improvement Measures Implemented

sections.label: SAF safety inspections and reviews
sections.summary: The IGO inspects safety policies, practices and incidents, and taps external experts and review panels, finding no significant systemic weaknesses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: The safety policies, management system and culture, day-to-day practices, compliance to training safety instructions and attention of commanders to safety outcomes form part of these inspections.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: In addition, the IGO also looks into notable safety incidents and near misses to establish their root causes, to determine if there are safety lapses and recommend corrective actions where necessary.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: In carrying out its work, the IGO also taps on external experts and review panels, including the External Review Panel on SAF Safety, which provides further independent reviews, benchmarking and recommendations on the SAF's safety management systems and practices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: While there have been no significant systemic weaknesses identified, the IGO recognises that the journey to zero accidents is a continuous one that requires constant effort to improve the safety culture for all units.

sections.label: SAF vehicle incident rate
sections.summary: From 2021 to 2023, the SAF vehicle incident rate decreased from 3.04 to 2.54 per 100,000 kilometres driven.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: From 2021 to 2023, vehicle incident rate in the SAF decreased from 3.04 per 100,000 kilometres driven in the work year 2021, to 2.54 in work year 2023.

sections.label: Heat safety measures and injuries
sections.summary: More heat sensors and a research centre were established, and annual heat strokes and heat exhaustion injuries fell from seven to two between 2021 and 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: More wet bulb globe temperature sensors have been installed in camps and training areas to provide real-time environmental heat measure for better work rest cycle decisions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: In 2023, the SAF partnered the National University of Singapore and the DSO National Laboratories to establish the Heat Resilience and Performance Centre to conduct research and development on soldier heat resilience and adaptation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How) (for the Minister for Defence)
sentences.text: Between 2021 and 2023, the annual number of heat strokes and heat exhaustion injuries has fallen from seven to two, with no heat strokes during that period.
